messages:
sam-support: Hey team, customer (AcmeAnalytics) opened an escalation — embeddings endpoint throughput dropped ~3x since yesterday evening. They say tokens/sec looks stable but vectors/sec is plummeting, and some requests are failing with a `400 dimension mismatch` and intermittent 429s. Sending logs and a simple repro below. Can eng-runtime or eng-ml take a quick look? :eyes:

jessica-cs: Customer shared traffic pattern: spike of small requests (single-doc, ~200 tokens) and some bulk imports (batch_size=64). They were on model `all-emb-1536-v2` and only changed client-side recently to send `batch_size` explicitly — but they rolled that back and still see the regression. Billing shows no throttles from our side.

sam-support: Repro curl they ran (redacted API key):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"all-emb-1536-v2","input":["doc1","doc2", ...],"batch_size":64}'
```

sam-support: Error snippets from their app: `400 Dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1537` (rare), and primarily high p99 latency on embeddings RPC (~2.6s -> 8s) with vectors/sec dropping ~70%.

sarah-eng-runtime: Thanks — pinging in thread. Two quick asks: 1) can you paste a couple of exact request payload headers (content-length + batch_size) from their recent failing requests? 2) Are they hitting Dedicated or Hosted?

jessica-cs: Hosted. I grabbed one header: `Content-Length: 20488`, `x-client-batch: 64`. Also they saw a surge at 01:12 UTC and after that latency increased.

mike-eng-ml: Dimension mismatch suggests client-side tokenization or concatenation bug, but that wouldn't explain vectors/sec drop across the fleet. My gut: batching behavior changed in the runtime (dynamic batching or queue depth) causing more small batches that are GPU-inefficient. Could be also kv-cache pressure if variant mapping changed.

arjun-eng-sre: I'm pulling metrics now. From infra: on the cluster serving `all-emb-1536-v2` around 01:10 UTC we saw GPU busy ~95%, GPU memory stable, but host-side queue depth spiked (per-instance request queue length + average batch size went down). That pattern -> many small batches saturating scheduling but not saturating SMs efficiently. Also a few nodes hit high `io_wait` in the vectorizer stage.

sarah-eng-runtime: Can you share the prom query results?

arjun-eng-sre: Paste of relevant metrics (trimmed):
```
avg(batch_size) by (instance) [5m] -> dropped from 28 -> 6
requests/sec by (instance) -> constant
gpu_utilization_sm -> 60-95% (fluctuating)
gpu_latency_p99 -> increased 3x
queue_length -> spiked from 2 -> 16 per instance
```

mike-eng-ml: This matches a throughput collapse where many tiny batches reduce vectors/sec because we don't amortize kernel launch cost. We should check if the batching service (batcher) recently deployed change to `flush_after_ms` or `max_batch_bytes` heuristics. Any deployments around 01:05-01:15?

deploy-bot: New rollout: `runtime/batcher` service deployed at 01:03 UTC -> roll/commit abc123 (change: adaptive flush tuning).

sarah-eng-runtime: Bingo. Let's roll the batcher back to previous commit on a single canary pool and measure. Also, we need to reproduce with a client that sends the same small single-doc requests to see queue behavior.

sam-support: Customer willing to run repro; they can send steady 10 rps single-doc for 10 minutes. Do we want logs or APM traces?

arjun-eng-sre: Yes — ask them to enable `X-Debug-Trace: 1` header so we can correlate request id -> instance. Also I'll attach an automated script they can run.

mike-eng-ml: Quick repro script (python):
```python
import requests, time
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer REDACTED','Content-Type':'application/json','X-Debug-Trace':'1'}
for i in range(600):
    r = requests.post(url, json={'model':'all-emb-1536-v2','input':['short doc']}, headers=headers)
    if r.status_code != 200:
        print('err', r.status_code, r.text)
    time.sleep(0.1)  # 10 rps
```

jessica-cs: Customer ran it for 10m. Attached trace ids: trace-7f3, trace-7f4, trace-7f5. They saw p95 jump after ~2m. Also captured one `400 dimension mismatch` with trace id trace-7f4.

sarah-eng-runtime: Arjun, can you correlate trace ids to instances and dump batch logs? Look for `batch_flush_reason` and `batch_size_observed`.

arjun-eng-sre: Correlated. trace-7f4 hit instance inst-a-03. Logs: several flushes due to `flush_timeout` with `observed_batch_size=1`. commit abc123 added a lower `flush_timeout_ms` to reduce latency for small requests, but it looks like under this traffic pattern it makes many single-item flushes which is killing throughput.

mike-eng-ml: That explains vectors/sec collapse. Why dimension mismatch though? If a single request was reassembled incorrectly across the batching boundary maybe a stray padding token or wrong join of batched vectors. Check batch assembly logic — maybe a fencepost bug with var-length encoded inputs introduced in that commit.

sarah-eng-runtime: I see commit abc123 touches both `flush_timeout` and a minor refactor in `pack_inputs()` where we handle utf8 boundaries. Could be that for very short payloads one caller path appended newline leading to extra token. But that wouldn't create 1537 vs 1536 unless tokenization differs between inference container and client. Still, there's a plausible path: a boundary bug appends a zero-width char causing token count to change. We'll revert flush_timeout change and run canary.

sam-support: Customer ok with canary. When can you revert?

sarah-eng-runtime: Rolling back now to commit def456 to the canary pool. Monitoring metrics for the canary...

(arjun-eng-sre): metrics 5m after rollback:
```
canary avg(batch_size) -> back to 26
canary vectors/sec -> +2.8x
canary p99 latency -> back to ~2.8s
host queue_length -> dropped to 3
```

mike-eng-ml: Looks promising. Ask customer to resume their import / synthetic load and get traces. Also add a job to run fuzz tokenization tests on inputs like NUL, zero-width joiner, soft-hyphen.

jessica-cs: Customer confirmed canary is good — vectors/sec back to normal and no more dimension mismatch in their short test. They asked what caused billing blips earlier — they got lots of errors & retries which triggered duplicate invoice lines; finance said it's safe and will dedupe.

sam-support: Great. Capture root cause: regression introduced by `runtime/batcher` commit abc123 that lowered `flush_timeout_ms` and refactored input packing; primary impact: many single-item batches -> throughput collapse; secondary: rare input packing edge-case led to a `dimension mismatch` when a tiny invisible char altered tokenization.

sarah-eng-runtime: Action items:
- (sarah) Revert rollout fleet-wide after validating canary for 30m.
- (mike) Add unit + fuzz tests for pack_inputs and tokenization edge-cases.
- (arjun) Create dashboard showing avg batch_size, queue_length, and vectors/sec for emb models; alert if avg_batch_size drops >50% vs baseline.
- (jessica) Communicate to customer: root cause, rollback timeline, and apology + invoice dedupe status.
- (sam-support) Keep thread updated with customer logs/incidents.

deploy-bot: Rollback started: `runtime/batcher` -> rolling to commit def456 (roll id r-4521)

arjun-eng-sre: One more note: when we changed flush_timeout it helped latency for tiny requests in isolation, but mixed workload (small + large imports) causes oscillation in batch sizes. We should build an adaptive rule that considers recent avg_batch_size and prefers higher thresholds when large-batch imports detected. Filing a design ticket.

mike-eng-ml: Agreed — I'll partner on the design ticket (TKT-8892). Also we should add a canary gate that compares vectors/sec/avg_batch_size pre/post and blocks flusher tuning changes if vectors/sec drops >30%.

jessica-cs: Customer asked for ETA on fleet rollback and confirmation once done. Will relay.

sam-support: Thanks all — marking as high priority. Will update after fleet rollback completes and customer test. :thumbsup:
